Update: Additional troubleshooting performed.

VRChat Settings checked:

- All Safety settings enabled (all friends)

- "Show Avatar" tested on individual players

- Avatar Performance Rank set to Very Poor

- All graphics settings set to maximum

- Allow Untrusted URLs: enabled

- Avatar Interactions: enabled

Launch options tried:

- -force-d3d11 → launches but no improvement

- -force-glcore → InitializeEngineGraphics failed

- -force-vulkan → InitializeEngineGraphics failed

- --disable-amd-stutter-workaround → no improvement

AMD Radeon Software settings checked:

- Anti-Lag: disabled

- Radeon Boost: disabled

- Image Sharpening: disabled

- Tessellation: AMD Optimized

- Color Enhancement: disabled

Driver versions tested:

- 26.10.21.05 (original) → no improvement

- 26.3.1 (downgrade) → no improvement

- 25.12.1 (downgrade attempt) → incompatible with RX 9060 XT,

  installation failed

Additional notes:

- Other players using the same avatars can see the emission effects

- Issue occurs regardless of world or avatar

- PICO 4 used as VR HMD via PC streaming

I have been experiencing this issue since I started playing VRChat 

in June 2026, and it has never improved. This greatly diminishes 

my experience in VRChat. 😢

Additional finding:

Not all emission effects are invisible. 

Some lighting effects are visible (e.g. event icons).

However, emission effects on avatars using lilToon shader 

are completely invisible.

This suggests the issue may be specific to lilToon shader 

compatibility with the RX 9060 XT.

I’ve been playing for a long time on both the RX 7900 XT and RX 9070 XT, and I have never encountered this issue.

I also use the PICO 4 with PICO Connect and Virtual Desktop, and everything works fine.

I’m not sure how the emission or glow effects look on your end, since there aren’t any screenshots or examples in your post. Just in case, here are a few things worth checking.

One setting that is easy to overlook is Bloom Intensity.

Could you check whether Bloom Intensity in VRChat is set to 0% or another very low value?

Please also verify this setting: Settings > Display and Visual Adjustments > Bloom Intensity.

Next, please confirm that AMD Software was installed correctly. The driver version 26.10.21.05 corresponds to Adrenalin Edition 26.6.4.

If the Current Version shown in the DRIVER & SOFTWARE section on the AMD Software home screen displays 26.10.21.05 instead of 26.6.4, then something is clearly wrong with the installation.

It may have been automatically installed through Windows Update, or an issue may have occurred during the installation process.

Also, when downgrading the driver, you should not simply install the older version over the existing one.

If you downgraded without using DDU, that alone can cause issues because leftover components from the previous driver may remain.

First use AMD Cleanup Utility or Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) to completely remove the current driver.

Boot Windows into Safe Mode, run DDU, and then perform a clean installation of either Adrenalin Edition 26.6.4 or 26.3.1.
